# Mining and shared gathering interfaces — GT-M source-authoring verdict

**Audience: internal conference record, not the player-facing projection.**

**Status: finite source/interface authoring decisions, not exact-card approval.** These decisions cover all **43 Mining originals, recipe-320–358 and recipe-656–659**. Mining contains **29 public, two restricted and twelve Director-only formulas**. Skinning and Salvaging receive only the shared constraints expressly identified below; their complete original records have not yet been supplied in this conference.

**Promotion authorized now: zero cards.** Current reviewed totals remain **392/687, with 295 remaining; public 251/433, with 182 remaining**. The 128 gathering-tool cards remain pending. Reconcile the three trade source verdicts before authoring their exact operational candidates, as requested.

## Evidence and authority

The source anchors in this verdict refer to the supplied text, not outside RPG rules:

- **S1:** Part A, `CRAFTING_HARVEST_PLAYTEST.md`, especially Training, Crafting check, Material identity, Identify and harvest, Preservation, and Salvage/research/sale.
- **S2:** Part A and Part B, `CRAFTING_TRADE_REFERENCE.md` and the current non-artisan trade/kit records.
- **S3:** Part A equipment and body/equipment guides, plus Part B’s ten exact equipment references.
- **S4:** Part A’s completed Fishing guide, used for its established identity, custody, chronology and cross-route boundaries—not as an automatic source of Mining durations, units or prices.
- **S5:** Part A, Core resolution, “Which rule applies” and “Rolls.” Specific crafting and dismantling exceptions remain specific.
- **S6:** Part B, the complete Mining COMMON/recipeOverrides originals, component occurrence references and structural register. Mechanical V4 source SHA-256: `32b2bf00c28584ad259c343bc5b961126d25078c094444c05bf3caf0c9edda5e`.
- **S7:** Part B’s 29 six-paragraph Mining V5 bindings. Supplied book SHA-256: `38eac505991a944ea557afa27751f510f773744734dc7a8e84c52b9bf7dcb099`.

Every provision marked **NEW** is an explicit authoring completion. Preserve original objects, absent/null distinctions, component occurrences, current and legacy effects, duplicated resultItem mechanics, discovery/access fields, statuses, guidance and source-book paragraphs. Never overwrite a source field to make it appear to have contained this verdict.

The supplied audit reports and hashes remain source evidence. This conference is not a fresh verification of repository bytes, protected-file hashes, prior Fishing tests or runtime behavior. The register below recalculates reserves and finished references from the supplied Mining fields and the newly selected body values.

## GT-M01 — Resolve all printed effects and all thirteen omissions

**Affected: all 43 Mining IDs. Source: S6; public text corroboration: S7.**

| Effect group | Exact recipes | Source check bonus | Operational mineral-quality step | Operational additional ordinary units |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| A | 320–344 | +1 | None | None; source extraYield remains 0 |
| B | 345–355, 656, 657 | +2 | One eligible unit on Success or Critical Success, under GT-M07 | **NEW:** up to one real reserve unit, on Critical Success only |
| C | 356–358, 658, 659 | +3 | One eligible unit on Success or Critical Success, under GT-M07 | Printed two additional units: up to two real reserve units, on Critical Success only |

The explicit omission disposition applies individually to **recipe-345, recipe-346, recipe-347, recipe-348, recipe-349, recipe-350, recipe-351, recipe-352, recipe-353, recipe-354, recipe-355, recipe-656 and recipe-657**. For each, preserve both original `extraYield:1` fields and the exact prose that omits yield. Adopt the number through a separately labeled **NEW critical-success-only recovery overlay**. Do not describe that trigger as recovered source wording.

This choice retains the positive data without inventing an ordinary-success yield. It also makes the two-unit critical clause a direct increase over the one-unit critical overlay. Neither quality nor additional yield operates on Failure/Critical Failure, prospecting, identification, assay or later processing. Details and physical limits follow below.

**NEW:** “one successful mineral harvest” means one completed finite extraction attempt, improving at most **one actual eligible ordinary mineral unit**, not every unit/category in the haul. The tool is reusable on genuinely different lawful attempts; this phrase creates neither a lifetime charge nor a daily refresh. An already resolved allocation cannot be harvested again to repeat the benefit.

Tags—including primary `mechanics.tag`—remain recipe identity in this trade. They do not require matching minerals and grant no affinity selection, elemental damage, resistance, heat, cooling, stealth, telepathy, Strength, protection, supernatural detection or cosmological authority. Historical spell-like/combat effects remain inactive. All four supplied wholeCreatureUse fields remain unchanged and grant no donor powers.

## GT-M02 — Credentials, check scope and bounded stacking

**Affected: all Mining recipes; shared credential constraints also bind later Skinning/Salvaging. Sources: S1–S3, S5–S6.**

Mining uses the **non-artisan Miner's-tools credential**. Owning any kit or enchanted output grants no proficiency, trade level, formula or free equipment. An artisan-only choice cannot select this credential. Forge Dwarf’s artisan creation time and quality benefits do not apply to manufacturing, using or repairing these Mining recipes.

**NEW eligible magical-bonus tasks:** the bounded mineral prospecting, mineral assay and mineral extraction procedures in GT-M04, and an independently authorized mineral-removal procedure using the same actual Mining credential and a compatible family role. A tool must physically perform the relevant operation. No bonus applies merely because the record says “Mining.”

**Excluded:** recipe creation, formula copying/research, item identification, creature-type knowledge identification, commercial valuation, refining/smelting, post-harvest dressing, gem/jewelry manufacture, preservation, dismantling, repair/reconstruction, navigation, combat and general obstacle clearing. A future exact rule may authorize another task; these cards do not.

Use one applicable proficiency contribution. Extraction chooses STR or WIS before work; the information procedures below use WIS. Applicable expertise replaces PB. **NEW explicit gathering binding:** untrained attempts use no tool PB and have disadvantage, but an unranked ordinary mineral task has no recipe-level gate. Missing tools, access or containment prevents work rather than merely imposing disadvantage. No trade level is added to a roll. Use the lead’s currently applicable ability and proficiency at resolution, not the tool maker’s, donor’s or a prior worker’s statistics.

**NEW Mining-only comparison families:**

| Family | Rule |
|---|---|
| `equipment.mining-task-enhancement` | Strongest independently eligible Mining recipe check bonus once; never sum these recipes |
| `equipment.mining-extra-recovery` | Strongest eligible critical-only extraYield once, against the finite reserve |
| `equipment.mining-quality-step` | At most one qualifying step on one eligible unit; multiple tools do not multiply steps or targets |

These are not universal strongest-modifier rules. A separately reviewed class, feature, facility or other item must meet its own exact predicate and stacking rules. Its existence neither creates eligibility nor automatically causes addition, replacement or cancellation. Do not move effects between established families to manufacture stacking. A genuine new cross-family conflict requires its actual source at final reconciliation.

The lead receives the Mining item effect only from their own actual operation. One eligible extraction assistant may provide the framework’s **+1**, with their own hands and actual full work time. Their item bonus does not transfer to the lead. Two +2 tools, one operated by the lead and one by the assistant, therefore provide **+2 equipment and +1 assistance**, not +4 equipment. Assistance never supplies the lead’s missing hands or an extra proficiency term. The new information procedures also permit at most one trained assistant, working their full duration for +1.

The trade-level-10 specialty remains the source’s **crafting-work-order** benefit. This conference does not extend it to field extraction.

## GT-M03 — Six explicit complete-body bindings

**Affected: the exact family sets below. Sources: S2–S3 and S6. All new dimensions, internal decomposition and non-source prices are NEW.**

All finished outputs are **durable magical nonartifact tools**, Standard equipment grade, with no attunement, charges, RP, concentration or separate magical activation. Each transforms an actual complete mundane body. There is no automatic size/grade scaling. Actual users still need compatible anatomy, sufficient handling capacity, working space and access.

| Code / body | Exact recipe IDs | Mundane value / empty mass | Ordinary structural HP / AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| P — Mining Pick | 322, 324, 328, 332, 343, 358, 656 | **2 gp / 10 lb**, binding the existing miner’s pick | 5 / 19 |
| G — Gem Cutter | 320, 334, 335, 339, 357 | **10 gp / 2 lb** | 5 / 19 |
| X — Ore Extractor | 321, 327, 336, 337, 345, 348, 349, 355, 659 | **8 gp / 4 lb** | 5 / 19 |
| T — Prospecting Tools | 323, 329, 330, 344, 351, 353, 354, 657 | **25 gp / 10 lb**, binding one actual Miner's-tools kit | 5 / 15 |
| S — Mining Tool | 325, 326, 331, 333, 338, 340, 341, 342, 346, 347, 350, 352, 356 | **5 gp / 3 lb** | 5 / 15 |
| D — Drill | 658 | **25 gp / 8 lb** | 5 / 19 |

**P — complete pick.** A 36-inch wooden shaft, 12-inch steel pick head and secured head-to-shaft fitting. Two manipulating hands operate it. It detaches actually workable exposed mineral material; it supplies no lifting multiplier, excavation rate, tunnel, weapon profile or wall-breaching result. Original head and shaft are primary constituents.

**G — complete manual cutter.** A 12 × 8 × 4-inch steel-framed, hand-operated scoring/chipping cutter with screw clamp, lever, cutting member and receiving tray. Maximum clamped specimen: **1 lb**, fitting a **4 × 4 × 2-inch** working space. Tray usable interior: **6 × 4 × 1 inch**, at most **1 lb and 0.01 ft³**. Both hands and an actual stable supporting surface are required. It can free or examine compatible mineral/crystal pieces; hardness and fracture behavior must support the operation. It does not guarantee that every gem can be cut. Original frame, clamp, lever and principal cutting member are required for magical reconstruction.

**X — complete manual extractor.** A 24-inch hand lever with steel extraction frame, wedge/jaw and retaining fittings; packed working envelope **24 × 8 × 6 inches**. It admits a supported workpiece up to **10 lb and 0.05 ft³**, fitting its **6 × 4 × 4-inch** jaw space. Two hands and real stable support are required. It frees accessible pieces by manual separation; it is not a hoist, autonomous machine, universal drill or containment vessel. Original frame, lever and extraction jaw are primary constituents.

**T — one complete prospecting kit.** The existing **25-gp, 10-lb** kit, not that kit plus a second free set. **NEW decomposition:** compact sampling pick 2 lb; sampling hammer 1 lb; sorting pan 1 lb; probe/chisel 0.5 lb; streak plate 0.5 lb; field lens 0.25 lb; fine probe/tweezers 0.25 lb; fitted case/trays 4.5 lb. Total **10 lb**. Closed case: **12 × 8 × 6 inches**; compact implements fit its fitted compartments. Two specimen wells each have a **2 × 2 × 1-inch** interior and limits of **0.25 lb and 0.002 ft³**. Contents add weight; wells provide no preservation or hazardous-essence containment.

The kit’s compact pick is a sampling implement, **not** the separate 10-lb catalog miner’s pick or the P output body. Its internal lens likewise receives no automatic profile, value or powers of the separate 100-gp magnifying glass or a tiered recipe lens. This resolves the mass conflict without altering either existing whole-kit or standalone-pick record. A suitable kit can satisfy the creation requirements for its actual included Pick and Assay kit. Work needing the full-sized pick still needs that actual implement. Kit contents are not independently guaranteed retail/salvage values.

The T kit supports two-handed sampling, measuring and selection. Its original sampling pick, hammer, pan, plate, lens and primary probe/chisel are the required primary set; the case and minor fittings may be replaced with physically compatible mundane parts without recreating a missing primary implement. A reconstructed kit still needs its complete ordinary contents.

**S — complete manual sorting tool.** A **12 × 12 × 4-inch** wooden sieve frame, **1/16-inch mesh**, separate solid receiving tray and brush. Tray interior **10 × 10 × 2 inches**, contents at most **5 lb and 0.10 ft³**. Empty masses: frame 0.75 lb, mesh 0.5 lb, tray 1.5 lb, brush 0.25 lb. Two hands operate it on actual supported material. Fines passing the mesh must enter a real tray, not disappear or become extra inventory. Original frame, principal mesh and tray are primary constituents; a brush may be replaced.

This is an explicit new binding of the current generic Mining Tool family. Preserve the six historical goggles names at **325, 326, 340, 342, 346 and 350**, and every historical sieve name, as inactive history. Do not silently grant eyewear, vision or protection, or create additional recipes from those names.

**D — complete manual drill.** An **18 × 8 × 6-inch** steel brace/frame, hand crank, chuck, **0.5-inch-diameter bit**, and support foot, with at most **6 inches of working penetration**. Both hands of one operator provide its power. There is no fuel-powered motor, battery, aura, unattended operation or automatic penetration rate. A compatible exposed mineral working face and actual support are required. Original brace/frame, crank/chuck and principal bit are primary constituents. An inaccessible seam does not become accessible merely because this model exists.

For all six models, specimen, tray and jaw limits are **handling limits, not output grants or per-hour production rates**. Serial loads may support a physically feasible work plan, but cannot shorten its required labor or multiply its allocation. Steel load-bearing bindings use AC19; the T/S whole-kit/frame bindings use AC15. Separately modeled exposed constituents retain their actual material defenses; naming a tiny component does not invent a cheaper Sunder target. Suppression does not change these physical HP/AC bindings. No model is automatically a weapon, focus or complete magical containment system. These imprints grant no magical-weapon damage classification to an improvised attack and no wearable AC candidate, including an AC-zero formula.

## GT-M04 — Concrete tasks and family roles

**Affected: all six families, within the following matrix. Sources: S1–S3, S5–S6; all new node procedures are NEW.**

| Family | Eligible prospecting | Eligible mineral assay | Eligible extraction role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mining Pick | No bonus | No bonus | Manual detachment of workable exposed mineral material |
| Gem Cutter | No bonus | Yes, when compatible scoring/examination is actually necessary | Controlled freeing/separation of compatible mineral or crystal specimens |
| Ore Extractor | No bonus | No bonus | Supported manual separation/recovery |
| Prospecting Tools | Yes | Yes | Sampling, measurement and selection actually performed as part of extraction |
| Mining Tool | No bonus | Yes, when actual sorting/examination is necessary | Screening and collecting actual mineral-bearing material |
| Drill | No bonus | No bonus | Manual boring needed to free a compatible exposed mineral piece |

**Prospecting:** ten active minutes, including setup, for one preregistered accessible survey patch of at most **100 ft² of exposed surface**. Use WIS/Mining. Declare DC **12** for clear accessible signs, **15** for mixed/obscured but assessable signs, or **18** for severe but feasible examination conditions. These are new Mining information DCs, not imported Fishing rules. Success identifies only real observable evidence and possible access within that patch. Critical Success supplies no extra deposit, material or automatic hidden detection. Failure provides no new reliable finding; Critical Failure adds only a hazard declared beforehand. Repeating unchanged evidence, changing worker or renaming the patch supplies no new roll. New exposure or a concretely different evidence-bearing method may justify another information attempt.

**Mineral assay:** one active minute of close examination of one exposed mineral manifest or actual sample, with compatible assay implements. Use WIS/Mining against the highest assessed tier’s existing tier DC, unless an exact source supplies its own assay DC. Success reveals supported mineral categories, relevant physical suitability and known handling/preservation requirements. It establishes neither a guaranteed market quote nor hidden magical powers. Failure reveals no hidden qualities. Critical Success gives no extra units or quality step. A destructive test requires its actual separately recorded sample debit; non-destructive examination creates no sample inventory. Further checks require new evidence/method/consultation, as with existing identification.

This new mineral assay does **not** replace the creature-type knowledge mapping, spell/item identification, or an explicitly required specialist assay. A mineral-classified creature ingredient is not thereby an environmental node. Mining of remains requires an independently applicable source permission and the ordinary remains procedure.

**Default exposed-node extraction:** one **60-active-minute** attempt: five minutes setup, fifty minutes of the actual detachment/separation workflow, and five minutes sorting, receipt and reconciliation. This bounded default admits one predeclared parcel of at most **50 lb gross handled material, including gangue, and 1 ft³**, already exposed and physically workable with the supplied apparatus. All selected baseline, reserve and damaged units must fit the workload and actual handling plan. Larger, inaccessible, structural, hazardous or technically incompatible work needs its own profile; there is no automatic cubic-foot/hour excavation promise.

Use STR or WIS/Mining, chosen beforehand. An exact applicable removal profile wins. Otherwise use the existing extraction DC ladder: **I 12, II 13, III 15, IV 16, V 18, VI 19**, determined by the highest desired selected material. The new quality label and tool recipe tier do not raise the material tier or alter that DC. No generic Tier VII–X harvesting right or DC is created.

A partial node harvest uses **ceil(60 × selected accessible categories / all accessible categories)** minutes, minimum one. This is the total time, not sixty plus another setup charge; apportion the necessary physical operations within it. Hurried work halves the applicable total, rounded upward to a whole minute, minimum one, with disadvantage. It must remain physically feasible. Where an existing remains/removal profile applies, retain that profile’s actual size time and partial/hurried arithmetic instead.

Tools operate manually during actual work. No unattended check, Fishing minute-55 schedule, five-minute landing stage, receipt duration or deployment allowance is imported. Every six seconds credited as

# Gathering-tool source audit — internal preparation

This evidence preserves **128 complete formulas**: Mining43, Skinning43 and Salvaging42; **82 public / six restricted / forty Director-only**. All82 public effects match exact V5 paragraphs. Eighteen checks pass across3,380 source-field comparisons. The only cross-version differences are128 absent V2 visibility fields. No formula effect or numeric conflict is resolved or approved here.

The **25 positive extraYield:1 data/prose omissions** are retained separately with both values and complete source text. Their presence across variants proves the discrepancy is stable, not whether the number should operate. The existing eleven Leatherworking AC conflicts have their own source disposition; that does not automatically settle these yield fields.

The128 formulas contain580 component occurrences:213 reusable tool rows,12 explicitly consumed tool rows and10 consumed catalyst rows. Preserve every occurrence, original quantity/tier/value and consumed flag. A costly high-tier tool input cannot silently become a cheap ordinary kit, and consumed=true cannot be corrected from its role name alone. Independently required credentials, facilities and actual tools remain distinct from process inputs. All work-hour values exist;54 field flags are true and74 false.

## Existing boundaries supplied for the eventual conference

The reviewed harvest procedure begins with a finite manifest: identities, tier, weight, value, total units, damaged recoverable allocation, anatomy and preservation. Base yield is rolled once. Partial selection forfeits unselected ordinary categories. Its four-degree extraction check can preserve one already-recorded damaged ordinary unit on Critical Success; it does not create an exceptional drop or exceed the original anatomy.

The reviewed basic dismantling route uses predeclared physically remaining mundane components,25% recovery and binary success at DC10. It irreversibly dismantles the item, and supplies no automatic magical/unique-item salvage profile or critical-success benefit. Consequently a Salvaging recipe's printed critical-success quality clause needs a specific compatible procedure; it cannot borrow another subsystem's critical rule silently.

Preservation condition (Fresh/Degraded/Spoiled), material tier, rarity, equipment grade, crafting outcome and a recipe's undefined “quality step” are different fields. No source name or common word proves they are interchangeable.

## Decisions required from GPT

- Resolve each of the25 unprinted extraYield1 fields explicitly, retaining source prose and data. If active, define trigger, cap, shared physical identity, frequency and interaction with printed extraYield2 critical clauses and the existing one-damaged-unit preservation rule.
- Define “quality step” separately for mineral harvest, hide/scale harvest and recovered mundane components. Preserve tier/access/rarity/value unless an explicit new rule changes a specific property; do not disguise an unbounded transmutation or multiplication of value as bookkeeping.
- Define actual eligible trade-check tasks: creation, identification, extraction, preservation, refining, dismantling, repair and research are not automatically one interchangeable roll. State which source bonus applies where and which real actor/tool use qualifies.
- Give complete finite body profiles for all seventeen named families, physical unit definitions, size/weight/value, material/HP, required stock or complete-body reservations, tool credential versus enchantment, and compatible use. A Tool/Kit/Rig name is not a free duplicate of an existing complete tool set or an equipment-grade upgrade.
- Resolve several enchanted tools, multiple workers, class/task modifiers and simultaneous body/gear use on one attempt. Give finite bonus/yield/quality arbitration without a universal strongest-modifier rule or repeated activation by transfer.
- Keep gatherable nodes/remains finite and previously manifested. No repeated failed/partial attempt, processing of already-recovered parts, recapture, item trade, repair, suppression or alternate worker may refresh the same anatomy/material allocation.
- For Salvaging, define percentages per actual remaining component identity and permitted unit precision, fractions/remainders, the quoted “up to” cap, failed work, critical-success procedure, and the relationship with the existing25% route. Do not add percentages or apply them to sale value. Magical/unique items still need actual salvage profiles.
- Address nested physical items and assemblies, contained supplies, unique embedded components, spent ammunition/charges, quality variants, source whole-creature references and catalysts. Recovery cannot include both an intact subassembly and its already-counted components.
- State whether quality improvement and extra yield require the tool at completion, the whole attempt, a selected phase or another explicit boundary. Cover damaged functional/Broken tools, suppression, meld, swapping and interruptions without reroll or duplicate claims.
- Preserve actual crafting abilities, primary credentials, station/access modes, field flags, assistants, phases, preservation and source triviality. Classify creation work against already reviewed artisan/non-artisan rules before applying Forge Dwarf; do not assume all crafted objects qualify.
- Decide explicit quality, persistent flaw, repair/reconstruction and value rules for these real bodies. Do not infer a charge, yield, quality-step, price or gear-grade increase from the generic structural-HP improvement option.

The [complete evidence](GATHERING_TOOL_SOURCE_PREPARATION.json) retains all128 originals,82 book bindings,25 omissions,225 tool occurrences,10 catalysts, all comparison differences and exact reviewed boundary paragraphs. It is unsent. Leatherworking's exact-card review remains active. No original information, worksite, body part, inventory resource or cosmology was changed by this audit.


ALL32 UNRESOLVED CASES
# Mining, Skinning and Salvaging — unresolved interface cases

Internal conference preparation only. These32 cases request decisions; they do not approve effects, replace original values, or alter existing harvest/dismantling rules. The128 complete sources and82 actual public-book bindings control what was printed. All17 family names need explicit physical bindings. Current reviewed guides must accompany the eventual conference.

| Case | Concrete situation | Decision needed |
|---|---|---|
| GT-01 | A character carries two +2 Mining tools, operates one and lends the other to an assistant. | Define actual-use predicates, the bonus family, strongest-versus-additive treatment, lead/assistant eligibility and interaction with the one proficiency application. Carrying alone and an assistant's mere possession must not silently benefit the lead. |
| GT-02 | A +3 tool is used to craft another tool of its own trade, research a formula, repair the old tool, and later extract material. | Enumerate which checks qualify. A printed trade bonus leaves these domains ambiguous; distinguish creating, prospecting, extracting, preserving, dismantling and repair. Avoid a self-reinforcing bonus without an explicit reviewed decision. |
| GT-03 | A class grants any artisan proficiency; a Forge Dwarf owns a Miner, Skinner or Salvager kit. | All three reviewed trade credentials are non-artisan. Resolve whether the ancestry's artisan creation benefit applies at all; do not inherit the Blacksmithing/Leatherworking reduction merely because these recipes manufacture tools. Preserve the class's actual choice restriction. |
| GT-04 | Recipe-322's consumed bill is one0.59-lb fang, yet Standard quantity is4 Mining Picks and maximum yield is6. | Specify supplemental complete bodies or quantified stock per output, their price/mass/structure, and ordered maximum reserves. A reusable source tool cannot become several free finished bodies. Preserve the actual component bill and its historical fields. |
| GT-05 | A maximum-yield reserve contains a damaged functional tool; it breaks before completion and another intact tool is available. | Specify when the work pauses, legal same-position replacement, latest completion HP, no post-roll cherry-picking, Failed/Mishap handling, unused-body returns and separation from fractional ingredient recovery. |
| GT-06 | A singleton Flawed tool receives a later durability upgrade and is then repaired twice. | Bind output quantity/structural durability to shared quality rules. Decide exact persistent-flaw and damage-deficit treatment, without turning quality into better recipe bonus, greater recovery, extra yield, higher source tier or additional catalysts unless explicitly directed. |
| GT-07 | A returned tiered Sorting pan is reused; recipe-657 instead lists that type of tool as consumed. | Retain each occurrence's actual quantity,tier,price and consumed flag. Decide kit/station overlap and whether any source correction is warranted. The audit's213 reusable and12 consumed tool rows must not be flattened into a universal tool policy. |
| GT-08 | Recipe-353 returns a catalyst on Masterwork while recipe-657 consumes tool rows that resemble durable implements. | Specify exact eligible catalyst selection and occurrence identity; the ten real catalyst rows are distinct from tool-role inputs. No tool or fuel receives catalyst recovery merely because it is expensive. Returned material cannot also be embodied in an output or salvaged from process waste. |
| GT-09 | A field-labelled formula has fieldCraftable:false; another has:true but the operator lacks its station or required implements. | Bind the actual recipe flag, access requirements, station portability, equipment completeness, phase boundary, elapsed versus active time, assistants and source triviality threshold. No label silently supplies a mine face, assay bench, rack or salvage table. |
| GT-10 | A magical tool is suppressed, reduced to0HP, partially lost from a multipart kit, stowed or melded. | Define each complete/functioning/actual-use state, mass and custody. Decide which ordinary functions survive suppression; no check bonus may imply usable missing implements, restored HP, an operating unattended machine or free hands. |
| GT-11 | A player repairs an intact damaged kit, reconstructs a Broken rig, or replaces a missing kit member. | Provide exact ability/proficiency/tools,station,time,DC,material reference and failure outcomes. Distinguish mundane body price from finished unit price and say whether repair grants XP, formula knowledge, quality rolls or creation discounts. |
| GT-12 | An owned base kit has an expensive source tool requirement and several finished units share one batch value. | State batch/Q once, supplemental body value, reusable-tool ownership/capital cost, purchase rounding and real buyer limits. No automatic buyback or conversion between current ingredient price and a legacy effect creates an economy loop. |
| GT-13 | A Mining formula has numeric extraYield:1 but printed effect only +2 checks and one quality step. | Dispose explicitly of all13 Mining omissions; source/resultItem values agree and are preserved. If adopted, declare a new overlay with trigger,unit identity,quantity cap and failure behavior. If deferred or rejected, retain the field as historical evidence. |
| GT-14 | A Skinning formula has the same unprinted extraYield:1, but a carcass has only one usable hide. | Dispose of all12 Skinning omissions separately from anatomical capacity. Do not infer that the Leatherworking AC precedent automatically adopts this yield. Name any new operational overlay and preserve the original prose. |
| GT-15 | A +3 Mining tool obtains critical success at a vein whose manifest has four ordinary units, two accessible now and two behind an obstruction. | Define the two printed additional units against a finite predeclared reserve, real extraction access, weight and time. Decide partial exhaustion and insufficient-yield outcomes; a successful check must not itself invent limitless geology. |
| GT-16 | Two miners work one vein in shifts; a player subdivides or renames the remaining deposit after a failed attempt. | Establish opportunity/deposit identity, shared depletion, retry policy, failure/time loss and discovery/prospecting versus extraction. Tool swapping, shift changes and subdividing records must not refresh a finite opportunity without an explicit procedure. |
| GT-17 | A successful mineral harvest contains ore, a damaged crystal and an exceptional named drop. | Define one quality step and the eligible target/count/timing. Distinguish condition, material grade, tier, rarity, sale quote and manufacturing outcome. Decide whether the printed word one affects a unit, category, check or entire harvest; it must not silently upgrade every component. |
| GT-18 | A Gem Cutter works a previously mined stone; a Prospecting Tools set searches for a deposit; an Ore Extractor harvests it. | Bind all six Mining families' ordinary task roles and exact bonus scope. # Mining and shared gathering interfaces — GT-M source-authoring verdict

**Audience: internal conference record, not the player-facing projection.**

**Status: finite source/interface authoring decisions, not exact-card approval.** These decisions cover all **43 Mining originals, recipe-320–358 and recipe-656–659**. Mining contains **29 public, two restricted and twelve Director-only formulas**. Skinning and Salvaging receive only the shared constraints expressly identified below; their complete original records have not yet been supplied in this conference.

**Promotion authorized now: zero cards.** Current reviewed totals remain **392/687, with 295 remaining; public 251/433, with 182 remaining**. The 128 gathering-tool cards remain pending. Reconcile the three trade source verdicts before authoring their exact operational candidates, as requested.

## Evidence and authority

The source anchors in this verdict refer to the supplied text, not outside RPG rules:

- **S1:** Part A, `CRAFTING_HARVEST_PLAYTEST.md`, especially Training, Crafting check, Material identity, Identify and harvest, Preservation, and Salvage/research/sale.
- **S2:** Part A and Part B, `CRAFTING_TRADE_REFERENCE.md` and the current non-artisan trade/kit records.
- **S3:** Part A equipment and body/equipment guides, plus Part B’s ten exact equipment references.
- **S4:** Part A’s completed Fishing guide, used for its established identity, custody, chronology and cross-route boundaries—not as an automatic source of Mining durations, units or prices.
- **S5:** Part A, Core resolution, “Which rule applies” and “Rolls.” Specific crafting and dismantling exceptions remain specific.
- **S6:** Part B, the complete Mining COMMON/recipeOverrides originals, component occurrence references and structural register. Mechanical V4 source SHA-256: `32b2bf00c28584ad259c343bc5b961126d25078c094444c05bf3caf0c9edda5e`.
- **S7:** Part B’s 29 six-paragraph Mining V5 bindings. Supplied book SHA-256: `38eac505991a944ea557afa27751f510f773744734dc7a8e84c52b9bf7dcb099`.

Every provision marked **NEW** is an explicit authoring completion. Preserve original objects, absent/null distinctions, component occurrences, current and legacy effects, duplicated resultItem mechanics, discovery/access fields, statuses, guidance and source-book paragraphs. Never overwrite a source field to make it appear to have contained this verdict.

The supplied audit reports and hashes remain source evidence. This conference is not a fresh verification of repository bytes, protected-file hashes, prior Fishing tests or runtime behavior. The register below recalculates reserves and finished references from the supplied Mining fields and the newly selected body values.

## GT-M01 — Resolve all printed effects and all thirteen omissions

**Affected: all 43 Mining IDs. Source: S6; public text corroboration: S7.**

| Effect group | Exact recipes | Source check bonus | Operational mineral-quality step | Operational additional ordinary units |
|---|---|---:|---|---|
| A | 320–344 | +1 | None | None; source extraYield remains 0 |
| B | 345–355, 656, 657 | +2 | One eligible unit on Success or Critical Success, under GT-M07 | **NEW:** up to one real reserve unit, on Critical Success only |
| C | 356–358, 658, 659 | +3 | One eligible unit on Success or Critical Success, under GT-M07 | Printed two additional units: up to two real reserve units, on Critical Success only |

The explicit omission disposition applies individually to **recipe-345, recipe-346, recipe-347, recipe-348, recipe-349, recipe-350, recipe-351, recipe-352, recipe-353, recipe-354, recipe-355, recipe-656 and recipe-657**. For each, preserve both original `extraYield:1` fields and the exact prose that omits yield. Adopt the number through a separately labeled **NEW critical-success-only recovery overlay**. Do not describe that trigger as recovered source wording.

This choice retains the positive data without inventing an ordinary-success yield. It also makes the two-unit critical clause a direct increase over the one-unit critical overlay. Neither quality nor additional yield operates on Failure/Critical Failure, prospecting, identification, assay or later processing. Details and physical limits follow below.

**NEW:** “one successful mineral harvest” means one completed finite extraction attempt, improving at most **one actual eligible ordinary mineral unit**, not every unit/category in the haul. The tool is reusable on genuinely different lawful attempts; this phrase creates neither a lifetime charge nor a daily refresh. An already resolved allocation cannot be harvested again to repeat the benefit.

Tags—including primary `mechanics.tag`—remain recipe identity in this trade. They do not require matching minerals and grant no affinity selection, elemental damage, resistance, heat, cooling, stealth, telepathy, Strength, protection, supernatural detection or cosmological authority. Historical spell-like/combat effects remain inactive. All four supplied wholeCreatureUse fields remain unchanged and grant no donor powers.

## GT-M02 — Credentials, check scope and bounded stacking

**Affected: all Mining recipes; shared credential constraints also bind later Skinning/Salvaging. Sources: S1–S3, S5–S6.**

Mining uses the **non-artisan Miner's-tools credential**. Owning any kit or enchanted output grants no proficiency, trade level, formula or free equipment. An artisan-only choice cannot select this credential. Forge Dwarf’s artisan creation time and quality benefits do not apply to manufacturing, using or repairing these Mining recipes.

**NEW eligible magical-bonus tasks:** the bounded mineral prospecting, mineral assay and mineral extraction procedures in GT-M04, and an independently authorized mineral-removal procedure using the same actual Mining credential and a compatible family role. A tool must physically perform the relevant operation. No bonus applies merely because the record says “Mining.”

**Excluded:** recipe creation, formula copying/research, item identification, creature-type knowledge identification, commercial valuation, refining/smelting, post-harvest dressing, gem/jewelry manufacture, preservation, dismantling, repair/reconstruction, navigation, combat and general obstacle clearing. A future exact rule may authorize another task; these cards do not.

Use one applicable proficiency contribution. Extraction chooses STR or WIS before work; the information procedures below use WIS. Applicable expertise replaces PB. **NEW explicit gathering binding:** untrained attempts use no tool PB and have disadvantage, but an unranked ordinary mineral task has no recipe-level gate. Missing tools, access or containment prevents work rather than merely imposing disadvantage. No trade level is added to a roll. Use the lead’s currently applicable ability and proficiency at resolution, not the tool maker’s, donor’s or a prior worker’s statistics.

**NEW Mining-only comparison families:**

| Family | Rule |
|---|---|
| `equipment.mining-task-enhancement` | Strongest independently eligible Mining recipe check bonus once; never sum these recipes |
| `equipment.mining-extra-recovery` | Strongest eligible critical-only extraYield once, against the finite reserve |
| `equipment.mining-quality-step` | At most one qualifying step on one eligible unit; multiple tools do not multiply steps or targets |

These are not universal strongest-modifier rules. A separately reviewed class, feature, facility or other item must meet its own exact predicate and stacking rules. Its existence neither creates eligibility nor automatically causes addition, replacement or cancellation. Do not move effects between established families to manufacture stacking. A genuine new cross-family conflict requires its actual source at final reconciliation.

The lead receives the Mining item effect only from their own actual operation. One eligible extraction assistant may provide the framework’s **+1**, with their own hands and actual full work time. Their item bonus does not transfer to the lead. Two +2 tools, one operated by the lead and one by the assistant, therefore provide **+2 equipment and +1 assistance**, not +4 equipment. Assistance never supplies the lead’s missing hands or an extra proficiency term. The new information procedures also permit at most one trained assistant, working their full duration for +1.

The trade-level-10 specialty remains the source’s **crafting-work-order** benefit. This conference does not extend it to field extraction.

## GT-M03 — Six explicit complete-body bindings

**Affected: the exact family sets below. Sources: S2–S3 and S6. All new dimensions, internal decomposition and non-source prices are NEW.**

All finished outputs are **durable magical nonartifact tools**, Standard equipment grade, with no attunement, charges, RP, concentration or separate magical activation. Each transforms an actual complete mundane body. There is no automatic size/grade scaling. Actual users still need compatible anatomy, sufficient handling capacity, working space and access.

| Code / body | Exact recipe IDs | Mundane value / empty mass | Ordinary structural HP / AC |
|---|---|---|---|
| P — Mining Pick | 322, 324, 328, 332, 343, 358, 656 | **2 gp / 10 lb**, binding the existing miner’s pick | 5 / 19 |
| G — Gem Cutter | 320, 334, 335, 339, 357 | **10 gp / 2 lb** | 5 / 19 |
| X — Ore Extractor | 321, 327, 336, 337, 345, 348, 349, 355, 659 | **8 gp / 4 lb** | 5 / 19 |
| T — Prospecting Tools | 323, 329, 330, 344, 351, 353, 354, 657 | **25 gp / 10 lb**, binding one actual Miner's-tools kit | 5 / 15 |
| S — Mining Tool | 325, 326, 331, 333, 338, 340, 341, 342, 346, 347, 350, 352, 356 | **5 gp / 3 lb** | 5 / 15 |
| D — Drill | 658 | **25 gp / 8 lb** | 5 / 19 |

**P — complete pick.** A 36-inch wooden shaft, 12-inch steel pick head and secured head-to-shaft fitting. Two manipulating hands operate it. It detaches actually workable exposed mineral material; it supplies no lifting multiplier, excavation rate, tunnel, weapon profile or wall-breaching result. Original head and shaft are primary constituents.

**G — complete manual cutter.** A 12 × 8 × 4-inch steel-framed, hand-operated scoring/chipping cutter with screw clamp, lever, cutting member and receiving tray. Maximum clamped specimen: **1 lb**, fitting a **4 × 4 × 2-inch** working space. Tray usable interior: **6 × 4 × 1 inch**, at most **1 lb and 0.01 ft³**. Both hands and an actual stable supporting surface are required. It can free or examine compatible mineral/crystal pieces; hardness and fracture behavior must support the operation. It does not guarantee that every gem can be cut. Original frame, clamp, lever and principal cutting member are required for magical reconstruction.

**X — complete manual extractor.** A 24-inch hand lever with steel extraction frame, wedge/jaw and retaining fittings; packed working envelope **24 × 8 × 6 inches**. It admits a supported workpiece up to **10 lb and 0.05 ft³**, fitting its **6 × 4 × 4-inch** jaw space. Two hands and real stable support are required. It frees accessible pieces by manual separation; it is not a hoist, autonomous machine, universal drill or containment vessel. Original frame, lever and extraction jaw are primary constituents.

**T — one complete prospecting kit.** The existing **25-gp, 10-lb** kit, not that kit plus a second free set. **NEW decomposition:** compact sampling pick 2 lb; sampling hammer 1 lb; sorting pan 1 lb; probe/chisel 0.5 lb; streak plate 0.5 lb; field lens 0.25 lb; fine probe/tweezers 0.25 lb; fitted case/trays 4.5 lb. Total **10 lb**. Closed case: **12 × 8 × 6 inches**; compact implements fit its fitted compartments. Two specimen wells each have a **2 × 2 × 1-inch** interior and limits of **0.25 lb and 0.002 ft³**. Contents add weight; wells provide no preservation or hazardous-essence containment.

The kit’s compact pick is a sampling implement, **not** the separate 10-lb catalog miner’s pick or the P output body. Its internal lens likewise receives no automatic profile, value or powers of the separate 100-gp magnifying glass or a tiered recipe lens. This resolves the mass conflict without altering either existing whole-kit or standalone-pick record. A suitable kit can satisfy the creation requirements for its actual included Pick and Assay kit. Work needing the full-sized pick still needs that actual implement. Kit contents are not independently guaranteed retail/salvage values.

The T kit supports two-handed sampling, measuring and selection. Its original sampling pick, hammer, pan, plate, lens and primary probe/chisel are the required primary set; the case and minor fittings may be replaced with physically compatible mundane parts without recreating a missing primary implement. A reconstructed kit still needs its complete ordinary contents.

**S — complete manual sorting tool.** A **12 × 12 × 4-inch** wooden sieve frame, **1/16-inch mesh**, separate solid receiving tray and brush. Tray interior **10 × 10 × 2 inches**, contents at most **5 lb and 0.10 ft³**. Empty masses: frame 0.75 lb, mesh 0.5 lb, tray 1.5 lb, brush 0.25 lb. Two hands operate it on actual supported material. Fines passing the mesh must enter a real tray, not disappear or become extra inventory. Original frame, principal mesh and tray are primary constituents; a brush may be replaced.

This is an explicit new binding of the current generic Mining Tool family. Preserve the six historical goggles names at **325, 326, 340, 342, 346 and 350**, and every historical sieve name, as inactive history. Do not silently grant eyewear, vision or protection, or create additional recipes from those names.

**D — complete manual drill.** An **18 × 8 × 6-inch** steel brace/frame, hand crank, chuck, **0.5-inch-diameter bit**, and support foot, with at most **6 inches of working penetration**. Both hands of one operator provide its power. There is no fuel-powered motor, battery, aura, unattended operation or automatic penetration rate. A compatible exposed mineral working face and actual support are required. Original brace/frame, crank/chuck and principal bit are primary constituents. An inaccessible seam does not become accessible merely because this model exists.

For all six models, specimen, tray and jaw limits are **handling limits, not output grants or per-hour production rates**. Serial loads may support a physically feasible work plan, but cannot shorten its required labor or multiply its allocation. Steel load-bearing bindings use AC19; the T/S whole-kit/frame bindings use AC15. Separately modeled exposed constituents retain their actual material defenses; naming a tiny component does not invent a cheaper Sunder target. Suppression does not change these physical HP/AC bindings. No model is automatically a weapon, focus or complete magical containment system. These imprints grant no magical-weapon damage classification to an improvised attack and no wearable AC candidate, including an AC-zero formula.

## GT-M04 — Concrete tasks and family roles

**Affected: all six families, within the following matrix. Sources: S1–S3, S5–S6; all new node procedures are NEW.**

| Family | Eligible prospecting | Eligible mineral assay | Eligible extraction role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mining Pick | No bonus | No bonus | Manual detachment of workable exposed mineral material |
| Gem Cutter | No bonus | Yes, when compatible scoring/examination is actually necessary | Controlled freeing/separation of compatible mineral or crystal specimens |
| Ore Extractor | No bonus | No bonus | Supported manual separation/recovery |
| Prospecting Tools | Yes | Yes | Sampling, measurement and selection actually performed as part of extraction |
| Mining Tool | No bonus | Yes, when actual sorting/examination is necessary | Screening and collecting actual mineral-bearing material |
| Drill | No bonus | No bonus | Manual boring needed to free a compatible exposed mineral piece |

**Prospecting:** ten active minutes, including setup, for one preregistered accessible survey patch of at most **100 ft² of exposed surface**. Use WIS/Mining. Declare DC **12** for clear accessible signs, **15** for mixed/obscured but assessable signs, or **18** for severe but feasible examination conditions. These are new Mining information DCs, not imported Fishing rules. Success identifies only real observable evidence and possible access within that patch. Critical Success supplies no extra deposit, material or automatic hidden detection. Failure provides no new reliable finding; Critical Failure adds only a hazard declared beforehand. Repeating unchanged evidence, changing worker or renaming the patch supplies no new roll. New exposure or a concretely different evidence-bearing method may justify another information attempt.

**Mineral assay:** one active minute of close examination of one exposed mineral manifest or actual sample, with compatible assay implements. Use WIS/Mining against the highest assessed tier’s existing tier DC, unless an exact source supplies its own assay DC. Success reveals supported mineral categories, relevant physical suitability and known handling/preservation requirements. It establishes neither a guaranteed market quote nor hidden magical powers. Failure reveals no hidden qualities. Critical Success gives no extra units or quality step. A destructive test requires its actual separately recorded sample debit; non-destructive examination creates no sample inventory. Further checks require new evidence/method/consultation, as with existing identification.

This new mineral assay does **not** replace the creature-type knowledge mapping, spell/item identification, or an explicitly required specialist assay. A mineral-classified creature ingredient is not thereby an environmental node. Mining of remains requires an independently applicable source permission and the ordinary remains procedure.

**Default exposed-node extraction:** one **60-active-minute** attempt: five minutes setup, fifty minutes of the actual detachment/separation workflow, and five minutes sorting, receipt and reconciliation. This bounded default admits one predeclared parcel of at most **50 lb gross handled material, including gangue, and 1 ft³**, already exposed and physically workable with the supplied apparatus. All selected baseline, reserve and damaged units must fit the workload and actual handling plan. Larger, inaccessible, structural, hazardous or technically incompatible work needs its own profile; there is no automatic cubic-foot/hour excavation promise.

Use STR or WIS/Mining, chosen beforehand. An exact applicable removal profile wins. Otherwise use the existing extraction DC ladder: **I 12, II 13, III 15, IV 16, V 18, VI 19**, determined by the highest desired selected material. The new quality label and tool recipe tier do not raise the material tier or alter that DC. No generic Tier VII–X harvesting right or DC is created.

A partial node harvest uses **ceil(60 × selected accessible categories / all accessible categories)** minutes, minimum one. This is the total time, not sixty plus another setup charge; apportion the necessary physical operations within it. Hurried work halves the applicable total, rounded upward to a whole minute, minimum one, with disadvantage. It must remain physically feasible. Where an existing remains/removal profile applies, retain that profile’s actual size time and partial/hurried arithmetic instead.

Tools operate manually during actual work. No unattended check, Fishing minute-55 schedule, five-minute landing stage, receipt duration or deployment allowance is imported. Every six seconds credited as
